newsitem.title: USA: Amer.Banknote undeterred by Verifact stance.
newsitem.headline: Amer.Banknote undeterred by Verifact stance.

text.p: American Banknote Corp said Thursday it would pursue additional avenues following the refusal of International Verifact Inc to meet to discuss a deal.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, American Banknote said it may boost its stake in Verifact by acquiring additional common shares or other securities, subject to favorable prices.
American Banknote holds a 6.36 percent stake in the Toronto-based company, or 447,500 common shares.

A series of exchanges between the two began in late November when American Banknote, in a letter to Verifact, said it wanted to meet to explore a "strategic transaction" that could enhance shareholder value.
L. Barry Thompson, president of the Canadian company, said a meeting was inappropiate. He cited a confidentiality agreement and a "no shop" provision that applies until December 30.
Thompson said his company was discussing with another corporation a possible global strategic alliance and other technology and business arrangements. The other corporation was not identified.
A "no shop" provision prevents a company from seeking better terms from any other corporation while it works out an agreement with a specific suitor.
Verifact makes payment systems for retailers, banks and governments. American Banknote, a New York-based company, is a check printing company.
